sprint: Magic Publish — Sprint M2 (Layer Decomposition Engine). Per docs/MAGIC_PUBLISH_ROADMAP.md: "Implement revealStages(slide). The function derives reveal stages purely from the final page. No history. No timeline." Stages: Blank -> World -> Artwork -> Decorations -> Text -> Finished, and "stages collapse automatically when empty."
task: js/magicReveal.js is rewritten from M1's single-stage stub into the real decomposition engine, behind the same revealStages(slide) -> [{slide,label,holdMs}] signature, so nothing downstream changed. Four beats are detected from the FINAL saved page only — world (the Theme Author's own Layer Pack furniture, scope-filtered exactly as _activeLayerPack filters it), artwork (slide.image or any _placeImages entry), decorations, text — and a beat with nothing to bring never produces a stage. The last arriving beat never gets a stage of its own either: that frame IS the finished page, so N beats yield N+1 stages and there is never a beat where nothing arrives. The final stage's slide is ALWAYS the caller's own object, so the finished frame is the real page rather than a reconstruction of it. A story-owned picture STICKER counts as a decoration, not artwork — the Artwork beat is the Place's own picture. Stripping is done on a clone: a shallow Object.assign plus deep copies of only the two bags a stage rewrites (metadata.elementOverrides, metadata.stickers), because slide.image is an HTMLImageElement and cannot be deep-cloned; the module never mutates the slide it is handed, which is what lets it run during Publish with zero risk to the page the child is looking at. Two strips cannot be expressed on the slide alone, so they became markers honoured by renderer/slideRenderer.js — the ~5 lines the architecture doc anticipated: _magicHideLayerPack (buildPayload resolves artworkTheme from ThemeEngine and ignores slide.artworkTheme, so filtering a cloned theme was rejected as reaching into shared module state; _activeLayerPack now returns null, its own established no-pack sentinel, which _hasSlideFullBleedFill already handles) and _magicSuppressPlaceholders (stripping the picture is precisely what makes the renderer fall through to its "Tap to add your artwork" dashed placeholder — real authoring chrome, and the one thing a Magic Creation must never show, product acceptance test 3). Three placeholder call sites were gated, not two: _drawPlaceOne, _drawPlaceExtra, and _v2DrawPlaceholder inside the V2 art layer. An ordinary payload carries neither marker, so both resolve false and every existing render is byte-identical. js/storyDestinations.js is deliberately untouched — it still encodes only the Finished stage, so Magic Publish's own output is unchanged by M2 and no publish regression is possible; drawing every stage is M3's job. Verified 33/33 via magic_m2_verify: beat detection across six page shapes; stage-list shape (four beats -> Blank/World/Picture/Decorations/Finished, two beats -> Blank/first/Finished, one beat -> Blank/Finished, nothing to reveal -> a single honest Finished frame, holds 750 with the finished page resting 2200); per-stage contents; the no-mutation guarantee across five page shapes including an existing elementOverrides bag; and decisive pixel-level proof both markers are real — a bright-green full-bleed Layer Pack fill paints on Finished and is genuinely GONE on Blank, an ordinary render still shows it, and a full-canvas diff between marker-on and marker-off clones exceeds 500 differing pixels. One test-methodology bug found and fixed in the suite, not an app bug: B6's own expectation contradicted B5's N+1 rule that had just passed on the same shapes (it asserted the one-beat outcome under a two-beat label), so it was corrected and a genuine one-beat case added.
